curations.textual_observation: Genesis repeatedly uses בְּרִית for the covenant with Noah and all living creatures.
curations.uncertainty: The term is broader than a single covenant form; the passage’s narrative and theological setting should not be generalized to every use of ברית.
curations.why: Genesis repeatedly uses בְּרִית for the covenant with Noah and all living creatures. This gives readers a passage-anchored connection from berit to What is Covenant? while preserving the authored direction.

curations.textual_observation: Hebrews 8 quotes Jeremiah 31:31-34 at length and interprets the new-covenant oracle within its argument about priestly mediation.
curations.uncertainty: This is an identifiable quotation and later reception, not proof that Jeremiah originally addressed Hebrews’ later theological questions or that the passage simply nullifies Israel’s covenantal identity.
curations.why: Hebrews 8 quotes Jeremiah 31:31-34 at length and interprets the new-covenant oracle within its argument about priestly mediation. This gives readers a passage-anchored connection from New Covenant Prophecy to Hebrews while preserving the authored direction.

curations.textual_observation: Jeremiah’s oracle promises a new covenant with Israel and Judah and describes instruction written on the heart and forgiveness.
curations.uncertainty: The oracle addresses a restoration context and does not by itself define all later uses of “new covenant” or erase its named Israel/Judah audience.
curations.why: Jeremiah’s oracle promises a new covenant with Israel and Judah and describes instruction written on the heart and forgiveness. This gives readers a passage-anchored connection from New Covenant Prophecy to Jeremiah while preserving the authored direction.
